report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of canary.py: module docstring and constants; claims and observations enumerated.
risks: canary.py:1-120 | medium | Module docstring claims egress/spend guarantees that depend on run_canary, vendors.council_env, and session.live_egress_seats; not verifiable in this chunk. | Cross-check run_canary and vendors in later chunks.

canary.py:95-99 | medium | Comment claims DEFAULT_BENCH_OLLAMA_HOST and DEFAULT_LOCAL_OLLAMA_HOST are exported, but they are only imported in this chunk; the local definitions are elsewhere. | Verify the import names match the exported names in vendors.

canary.py:110-121 | low | __all__ includes names (e.g., PROBES, QUICK_PROBE) not defined in this chunk; a typo in __all__ would silently break star-imports. | Confirm each name in __all__ is defined later in this file or imported.

canary.py:132-140 | medium | CANARY_STATUSES docstring says 'CLOSED' but nothing in this chunk enforces that; a later assignment could violate it. | Check for any mutation of CANARY_STATUSES in later chunks.

canary.py:142-146 | medium | SEVERITIES docstring says only liveness trips exit code, but the exit-code logic is in run_canary, not visible here. | Verify run_canary uses SEVERITIES and FAILING_STATUSES as documented.

canary.py:158-160 | medium | DEFAULT_OLLAMA_MODEL comment says 'qwen2.5-coder:7b' is cheapest sensible; not verifiable without vendor model availability. | Check vendor docs or configuration for model pricing/availability.

canary.py:180-183 | medium | new_nonce docstring says fresh per probe per lane, but call sites are not visible here; a reused nonce would violate the claim. | Inspect probe construction in later chunks for nonce reuse.

canary.py:188-193 | medium | _rng docstring says build and check agree, but that depends on both using _rng with the same nonce; not verifiable here. | Check build_* and check_* functions in later chunks for consistent nonce use.

canary.py:196-207 | medium | Comments claim _TAIL_WORDS is disjoint from _FILLER_WORDS and _ANCHOR_SETS are disjoint, but only _TAIL_WORDS vs _FILLER_WORDS is verifiable; the anchor sets are not compared to the filler words. | Programmatically compare the tuples for any overlap.

canary.py:207-209 | medium | _ANCHOR_SETS docstring/comment implies disjointness, but no explicit comment; the sets look disjoint but not guaranteed. | Verify each set's elements are unique across all sets.

canary.py:214-216 | medium | Comment says comprehension summaries may not contain 'roll'/'revert', but the code for that is cut off; not verifiable here. | Check the rest of _COMPREHENSION_SUMMARIES and the checker.
canary.py:1-120 | low | Module docstring describes an incident and design decisions; some claims are historical and cannot be verified from code. | Treat as narrative, not checkable facts.
todos: Verify in later chunks that run_canary defaults live=False and raises LiveCanaryRefused for shipped transports.
Verify that dry_run_plan prints the plan without dispatching and refuses --live --dry-run.
Verify that live_egress_lanes maps Lane to adapters and uses session.live_egress_seats.
Verify that build_* and check_* functions use _rng and new_nonce consistently.
Verify that the COMPREHENSION_SUMMARIES list is synthetic and excludes 'roll'/'revert'.
Verify that the exit code logic uses FAILING_STATUSES and SEVERITIES as documented.

handoff.purpose: Module docstring, closed vocabularies, constants, nonce and probe corpus definitions.

symbols.name: CANARY_STATUSES
symbols.note: Tuple of five probe outcome statuses: ok, wrong_answer, timeout, unavailable, error.

symbols.name: SEVERITIES
symbols.note: Tuple of two severity levels: liveness, quality.

symbols.name: FAILING_STATUSES
symbols.note: Frozenset of statuses that count as failure: wrong_answer, timeout, error.

symbols.name: SCHEMA_VERSION
symbols.note: String 'dcanary/1' for history schema version.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_HISTORY_PATH
symbols.note: Default path to history JSONL: runs/canary/history.jsonl.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_PER_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S
symbols.note: Default per-probe timeout in seconds: 120.0.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_WALL_CLOCK_S
symbols.note: Default wall-clock budget in seconds: 420.0.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_MAX_PARALLEL
symbols.note: Default maximum parallel lanes: 4.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_OLLAMA_MODEL
symbols.note: Default local Ollama model: qwen2.5-coder:7b.

symbols.name: VENDOR_KEYS
symbols.note: Tuple of vendor keys: anthropic, openai, google, local.

symbols.name: REPLY_TRIM
symbols.note: Maximum characters of a reply kept on record: 400.

symbols.name: TRAILING_WINDOW
symbols.note: Trailing window for median comparison: 20.

symbols.name: SLOWER_RATIO
symbols.note: Ratio threshold for material slowdown: 2.0.

symbols.name: SLOWER_ABS_S
symbols.note: Absolute seconds threshold for material slowdown: 2.0.

symbols.name: _NONCE_RE
symbols.note: Compiled regex matching NONCE- followed by 8 uppercase alphanumerics.

symbols.name: new_nonce
symbols.note: Returns a fresh nonce string starting with 'K' followed by 7 hex chars.

symbols.name: _rng
symbols.note: Returns a random.Random seeded deterministically from the nonce.

symbols.name: _FILLER_WORDS
symbols.note: Tuple of synthetic filler words for prompt padding.

symbols.name: _TAIL_WORDS
symbols.note: Tuple of tail words disjoint from filler words.

symbols.name: _ANCHOR_SETS
symbols.note: Tuple of triples of fruit names for anchoring probes.

symbols.name: _ORDINALS
symbols.note: Tuple of ordinal strings: first, second, third.

claims.text: EVERY PROBE IS (prompt, checker) AND THE CHECKER IS DETERMINISTIC PYTHON.
claims.why: The chunk defines constants and nonce helpers but does not show probe construction; the checker functions are named in __all__ but not defined here.

claims.text: No model judges another model's answer.
claims.why: No probe code in this chunk; the claim depends on check_* functions defined later.

claims.text: ``unavailable`` ... is NOT a failure and never trips the exit code.
claims.why: FAILING_STATUSES excludes 'unavailable' (line 148), but the exit-code logic is in run_canary, not visible here.

claims.text: :data:`CANARY_STATUSES` is closed
claims.why: The tuple is defined as a constant (line 135), but nothing in this chunk prevents reassignment elsewhere; closure is a policy not enforced here.

claims.text: :meth:`CanaryRun.summary` reports the two groups separately, by construction.
claims.why: CanaryRun is not defined in this chunk; summary method not visible.

claims.text: ``arrival`` and ``instruction`` ask ... that is LIVENESS, and a regression there is an alarm.
claims.why: Probe builders/checkers are not defined in this chunk; the severity classification is not visible.

claims.text: ``anchoring`` and ``comprehension`` ask ... that is QUALITY ... reported loudly and does NOT trip the exit code.
claims.why: Quality probes and exit-code logic are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: every host is passed EXPLICITLY per call; this module never sets, mutates or exports ``OLLAMA_HOST`` into any process environment
claims.why: No code in this chunk sets environment variables; the claim concerns run_canary and probe functions in later chunks.

claims.text: only ``127.0.0.1``/``localhost`` counts as local.
claims.why: The local-host predicate is in session.live_egress_seats, imported but not defined here.

claims.text: every probe body is synthetic -- generated filler, fruit names and invented one-line summaries.
claims.why: The probe corpora defined here are synthetic, but the claim about every probe body depends on build_* functions in later chunks.

claims.text: there is no code path here that reads a repo file.
claims.why: No file reads in this chunk, but the claim covers the whole module; later chunks may read files.

claims.text: :mod:`daedalus.council.vendors` already puts the prompt on stdin, kills the whole process tree on timeout, strips ``OLLAMA_HOST`` and refuses an over-budget Ollama prompt
claims.why: The vendors module is imported but not visible in this chunk; the claims about its behavior cannot be verified here.

claims.text: This module reuses those adapters and adds only what a canary needs on top of them.
claims.why: Adapter usage is in later chunks; this chunk only imports adapters.

claims.text: a bare ``daedalus canary`` used to spawn ``claude`` and ``codex`` ... with nothing asking first.
claims.why: Historical incident; not code in this chunk.

claims.text: ``--dry-run`` was an OPT-OUT, and an opt-out is not a gate
claims.why: Historical claim about past behavior; not code in this chunk.

claims.text: :func:`run_canary` takes ``live`` and it DEFAULTS TO FALSE.
claims.why: run_canary is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Any lane still carrying a shipped vendor transport raises :class:`LiveCanaryRefused` before a thread is started, before a probe is built and before one byte is dispatched.
claims.why: LiveCanaryRefused is imported from session but the raising logic is in run_canary, not visible here.

claims.text: The classification is :func:`session.live_egress_seats` -- IMPORTED, not re-implemented.
claims.why: The import is visible (line 111), but the claim about classification is about run_canary usage, not visible here.

claims.text: :func:`live_egress_lanes` only maps a :class:`Lane` back to the adapter(s) behind its ``ask`` callable and hands them to that one function.
claims.why: live_egress_lanes is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: The operator's form is ``daedalus canary --live``. Without it the CLI refuses and points at ``--dry-run``; ``--dry-run`` prints the plan, calls nothing, and NAMES THE SEATS ``--live`` would call
claims.why: CLI behavior is in a different module (likely __main__ or cli), not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``--live --dry-run`` together is REFUSED as ambiguous
claims.why: CLI parsing is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A fresh probe nonce, e.g. ``K7F3A9C1``.
claims.why: new_nonce returns 'K' + 7 uppercase hex chars; 'K7F3A9C1' is a possible output.

claims.text: Fresh PER PROBE PER LANE, not per run: a reused nonce cannot distinguish a lane that answered from a lane (or a cache, or a shared transcript) that echoed somebody else's answer
claims.why: The function returns a fresh nonce each call, but the claim about per-probe-per-lane usage depends on call sites in later chunks.

claims.text: Deterministic per-nonce randomness, so ``build`` and ``check`` agree.
claims.why: _rng is deterministic for a given nonce, but the agreement between build and check depends on both using _rng with the same nonce; not visible here.

claims.text: The prompt varies every run (a probe a model has memorised measures nothing) while the checker still knows the right answer without carrying state between the two halves of a probe.
claims.why: This depends on build_* and check_* functions using _rng consistently; not visible here.

claims.text: Disjoint from :data:`_FILLER_WORDS` on purpose: the arrival tail token must not be findable anywhere in the padding
claims.why: Comparing the two tuples in this chunk, no word appears in both _FILLER_WORDS and _TAIL_WORDS.

claims.text: Invented one-line summaries. None of these describes a real file in this repo, and none of them may contain 'roll'/'revert'
claims.why: The summaries list is cut off in this chunk; the claim cannot be checked.

observations.what: The module docstring makes several claims about run_canary, live_egress_lanes, and CLI behavior that are not verifiable in this chunk.
The __all__ list includes names like PROBES and QUICK_PROBE that are not defined in this chunk; they may be defined later in the file.
DEFAULT_BENCH_OLLAMA_HOST and DEFAULT_LOCAL_OLLAMA_HOST are imported from vendors but not defined locally; they are exported in __all__.
CANARY_STATUSES is documented as 'CLOSED' but the code only defines a tuple; nothing in this chunk prevents reassignment.
The nonce format is 'K' + 7 hex chars, but the example 'K7F3A9C1' has 7 characters after 'K'; the code produces exactly 7 chars from token_hex(4) which is 8 hex chars, sliced to 7.
The ANCHOR_SETS are fruit names; they appear disjoint from each other but there is no explicit comment or enforcement of disjointness.
